description.narrative: An increasingly peaceful political and social development in Ghana within a more peaceful region

The Project’s objective is to contribute to an increasingly peaceful political and social development in Ghana within a more peaceful region. The main project outcome is local and national response structures developed and feeding into National Early Warning and Response Systems and ECOWAS – Early Warning and Response System.
The engagement comprises core support to WANEP and earmarked support to NPC, with WANEP as the Embassy’s direct partner taking responsibility for financial management and reporting among other things. The core funding to WANEP will be used on implementation of WANEP’s ongoing 5-year strategy 2016 – 20 and from 2021, of the successor strategy 2021 – 2025 currently under preparation. The funds will be used on any activity falling within these strategies and the associated annual plans. WANEP’s upcoming strategy will, in addition to the current themes of the current strategy (national early warning and response systems; citizen capacity in peacebuilding and conflict prevention; utilising research to policy advocacy; gender capacity in peace building and conflict prevention deployment; and ensuring the institutional and financial sustainability of WANEP), feature new focus areas. These include targeted efforts to the youth, the relationship between conflict and environment/climate change, new approaches to gender peace and security, and the role of communities in conflict prevention and peacebuilding. WANEP is expected to i.a. plan and carry out a number of activities in collaboration with NPC in order for both to benefit from the complementarity between the two and in order for Ghana to benefit more from the expertise and regional perspective of WANEP.
